ev.q: The overall age-adjusted U.S. death rate decreased by 5.3% from 2021 to 2022.
The total number of deaths peaked during the weeks ending January 22, 2022 (85,405 deaths)
The age-adjusted rate, 832.8 deaths per 100,000 standard population, represented a decrease of 5.3% from 879.7 in 2021
Provisional* number and rate of total deaths and COVID-19–associated deaths, by demographic characteristic
COVID-19 was the underlying cause for 5.7% of all deaths in 2022
Age-adjusted death rates were higher among males compared with females in 2021 (1,048.0 and 733.3, respectively)
The changes in overall death rates for age groups <1 year and 5–14 years were not significant.
Age-adjusted death rates were calculated for deaths overall and by sex and race and ethnicity.
Age-adjusted death rates differed by race and ethnicity and decreased for all groups from 2021 to 2022.
NCHS analyzed provisional NVSS death certificate data for deaths occurring among U.S. residents
The trends in deaths during the year were determined by calculating the number of deaths for each week from all causes and from COVID-19.
